chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from 'Inbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Three things for which God has not granted anyone an excuse: Kindness to parents, whether they are righteous or wicked; Fulfillment of the covenant/promise, whether to the righteous or the wicked; And fulfilling the trust, whether to the righteous or the wicked.

key_terms.وَفَاءٌ بِالْعَهْدِ: Fulfillment of the covenant or promise

ai.seo_question: What three duties in Islam must be fulfilled even if the other party is wicked?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three duties as absolute obligations (wajib) where the moral status of the recipient does not mitigate the duty of the actor, distinguishing them from conditional acts of kindness. This underscores the Shia principle that filial piety, covenant-keeping, and trustworthiness are intrinsic virtues of the believer, independent of the recipient's righteousness or wickedness. The hadith serves as a theological safeguard against using others' flaws as excuses for one's own negligence in core religious duties.
